subject: Tenant keystore evacuation & rotation scenarios
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tenant keystore evacuation & rotation scenarios

Team —

After the last ops review with Acme (see INFRA-2145), I sketched three practical evacuation/rotation scenarios for private (VPC/on-prem) tenants that we need to validate for the cutover runbook. Attached: evacuation_matrix.xlsx and the first draft rotation-playbook-v1.md plus a network diagram. TL;DR options:

1) Customer-generated keys (BYOK on-customer-HSM) + Redwood-wrapped backup: customer creates keys inside their HSM; we accept wrapped-key imports for our sealed-operator fallback. Minimal exposure but complicates emergency rotation.
2) Redwood-provisioned tenant keystore inside customer VPC (HSM-backed) with split custody operator keys: we manage lifecycle but require operator quorum + customer approver for key unwraps. Easier for fast rotation but higher trust perimeter.
3) Sealed-bridge model: ephemeral wrapping keys generated in a sealed, network-isolated operator subnet (no egress) and escrowed with multi-party escrow (customer + 3rd-party escrow vendor). Good for disaster recovery, more operational overhead.

Key considerations I want us to confirm:
- Operator evacuation: step-by-step for sudden operator eviction (force-zeroize vs escrow-recover)
- Network profiles: required firewall rules, NAT/Bastion constraints, mTLS peer certs for the bridge
- Audit/telemetry: what we log locally vs. what the customer requires for SOC2 evidence (KMS access logs, signing events)
- Rotation cadence and live-rollover: strategies for zero-downtime rotations for long-lived KV caches and pinned model versions
- Attestation and proof-of-control: how we capture HSM attestation artifacts and persist them to the audit trail before any import/export

Please review the matrix and call out any red lines. Suggest we pick one primary path + one emergency fallback and run a tabletop in the week of 12/13.

Next asks:
- Hannah: can you confirm the minimum operator-quorum (# of keys & roles) and the hard-zeroize procedure?
- Kimberly: can you run a quick query on required egress ports for our HSM providers (nCipher/Thales) inside customer VPCs?
- Tessa: can we map the runbook steps to existing rollout automation (playbooks in ops-runner)?
- Monica: legal/security — anything obvious we should avoid for customer-managed BYOK?

Markus
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evacuation_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), rotation-playbook-v1.md (markdown), network-keystore-arch.png (diagram)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenant keystore evacuation & rotation scenarios

Thanks Markus — good breakdown. A few quick notes from ops/security perspective: 

- Operator quorum: minimum 3 distinct operator keys for any split-custody unseal, with at least two on different admin VMs/regions. That gives us tolerance to one operator lost and one AZ outage. I recommend policy: quorum 3, threshold 2 for normal unseal; emergency unseal must require customer consent + M-of-N escrow retrieval.
- Hard-zeroize: document must include USB and HSM tamper steps (for on-prem), and an API-driven remote zeroize for virtualized HSMs (clear signed event to audit).
- Audit telemetry: we must persist signed attestation blobs to a tamper-evident store (append-only), separate from primary logs. Suggest we use the dedicated audit bucket in customer's account (read-only to Redwood) to satisfy evidence requirements.
- Live rotation: use wrapping-key rolling where active key is wrapped by the next key, update pointers atomically in the config service. For long-lived KV caching, we need a cache-invalidation window and an edge-fallback to the older key for 5 minutes to avoid token failure spikes.

I will add these to rotation-playbook-v1.md and push an updated doc by EOD. Also, I flagged a compliance question for Legal: whether we can require customer-signed attestation before any key import if this is required by their auditors.

Hannah
Head of Infra Security

Subject: Re: Tenant keystore evacuation & rotation scenarios

Markus / team —

Thanks for the clear options. A couple items from Acme's side before the tabletop:

- For BYOK we prefer to generate keys in our nCipher appliance and provide a wrapped transfer. Does Redwood have a validated import pipeline for wrapped keys that preserves attestation and does not require us to disclose raw key material?
- In the sealed-bridge scenario: what guarantees do we provide around escape-hatches? If Acme needs emergency access (legal or regulator-driven), what is the expected time-to-recover and what evidence would we provide?
- On escrow: would you use a 3rd-party escrow vendor or Redwood-run escrow? We have a vendor (SecureVault) we trust; would combined escrow (customer + vendor + Redwood) make sense?

Would be great to see a short matrix (import/attestation accepted? time-to-recover goals? audit evidence) tailored to each option. Happy to host the tabletop and provide our audit team.

—Lydia
Head of Cloud Security, Acme Payments

Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenant keystore evacuation & rotation scenarios

Lydia — thanks, great questions. Quick replies and action items: 

- Wrapped-key import: yes — we support wrapped imports from customer HSMs provided the wrapped blob includes HSM attestation (certificate chain). We will not request raw key material. I'll attach an import checklist to the playbook; Kimberly will validate ports for nCipher/Thales flows.
- Emergency escape-hatch & time-to-recover: our recovery SLAs depend on model chosen: 
  * BYOK (customer HSM + wrapped import): recovery is dominated by customer churn and escrow retrieval — target 8–24 hours for legal-driven access with escrow route and documented chain-of-custody.
  * Redwood-provisioned (HSM inside customer VPC): with split-custody operator quorum + documented on-call runbook, target 2–6 hours for recovery (we control more steps).
  * Sealed-bridge + 3rd-party escrow: target 4–12 hours depending on escrow vendor SLA and approved authorizations.

- Escrow model: we are open to combined escrow (customer + SecureVault + Redwood). Bryan (cc'd) — can you confirm SecureVault's SLA and evidence package?

Action items: 
- Kimberly: validate HSM egress/port matrix for nCipher and Thales (deliverable: port-matrix doc) — due 12/07.
- Hannah & I: finalize operator-quorum proposal and emergency zeroize steps — deliverable: section in rotation-playbook-v1.md — due 12/09.
- Monica: review legal constraints on attestation preconditions and prepare a short list of redlines — due 12/08.
- Bryan: confirm escrow SLAs and what audit artifacts they can produce — due 12/09.

We'll use the Drive folder (linked) for updated artifacts. Lydia — happy to run the tabletop on the week of 12/13; please propose times and we'll pull in legal and Acme's audit team.

Thanks all —

Markus
Director, Platform Security

Attachments: updated rotation-playbook-v1.md (versioned), evacuation_matrix.xlsx (v2), network-keystore-arch.png (annotated)
